solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Curry favour with detectives in quad

parts.note: to court someone is to seek their favour
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

explanation.surface: Detectives gather in a college quad while someone sucks up to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A quad, short for quadrangle, is an enclosed open space surrounded by buildings, which is exactly that kind of yard.

clue.text: Head covering worn by neutered male fowl?

parts.note: a cap is worn on the head

explanation.surface: A castrated cockerel sporting a little hat, a deliberately silly image.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a cockerel castrated to fatten it for the table, so a gelded male bird.

clue.text: Ruin arrangements — disrupt Shaw's drama

parts.note: The Apple Cart is a 1928 political comedy by George Bernard Shaw

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks the plans by sabotaging a production of a Shaw play.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spoiling a plan or carefully settled state of affairs, like tipping over a stall of fruit.

clue.text: Freely do it in art — it's the custom

indicators.note: done freely, the letters are not held to their printed order

explanation.surface: An artist's advice: express yourself freely, as convention allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a long-established custom or practice handed down through generations.

clue.text: As an anchor may be? Not at home, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: someone not at home is away

explanation.surface: A sailor is out at sea, away from home, with the anchor raised.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is described this way when it has just been lifted clear of the seabed so the ship can sail.

clue.text: Police officer's rank and temperament

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; with the 's added
a rank is a position in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A report on a police officer's grade and character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's disposition is their natural temper or mood, the characteristic way they tend to feel and behave.

clue.text: Sea creature grandad accommodates for all to see

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house a guest, so one piece is put up inside the other

parts.note: an informal name for a grandfather
U is the film certificate for a universal audience

explanation.surface: Grandad puts up a sea creature at his house where everyone can see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The grampus is a dolphin-like cetacean, Risso's dolphin, also used of the killer whale.

clue.text: Plentiful information on leader of union in love

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: in places one piece within the following one

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A lover's ample knowledge about a trade-union leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous can mean ample or abundant, as in a generous helping, so it matches plentiful.

clue.text: Song that is covered by Garfunkel cheers

indicators.note: something covered by another thing has that thing around it

parts.note: Art Garfunkel, of Simon and Garfunkel
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A cover version of a song by Art Garfunkel, greeted with applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Garfunkel's first name is the piece that does the covering, not the singer's material.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short light aria, a small song in an opera or similar work.

clue.text: Husband allowed European in to indulge maker of leaflets

indicators.note: in places those pieces inside the next word's equivalent

explanation.surface: A husband lets a European in to spoil a pamphlet writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphleteer writes and publishes pamphlets, short polemical booklets, which are much like leaflets.

clue.text: Decorating technique of crooks in GBS

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the second

explanation.surface: Shaw's plays feature crooks who practise some decorative craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is the sailors' craft of carving or engraving designs on whalebone or ivory.

clue.text: Give the game away regarding marijuana

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inform on someone to the police

explanation.surface: Someone spills the beans about a drug deal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to inform, betraying a secret; as a noun it is common slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Old lady going over commercial area in Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece going over the next sits above it

explanation.surface: A granny reviewing an advert for a district in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, famous for the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: Friend in military intelligence taken in in the past

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside another thing

parts.note: MI abbreviates Military Intelligence, as in MI5

explanation.surface: A friend in the intelligence services who was once fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like deceived, but it is placing one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English too.

clue.text: Sugar substitutes offered as bribes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: artificial products used instead of sugar
second meaning: inducements that make a deal more attractive

explanation.surface: Artificial sugar handed over as backhanders.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is literally a sugar replacement and figuratively an inducement or payment to win someone over.

clue.text: Journey made by son in Dad's time

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A son retraces a journey his father made long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a voyage or crossing, especially by sea, so a journey.

clue.text: Mount rearmost of horses in major road

indicators.note: the rearmost part is the very end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the A1, Britain's longest road, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Riders mount up on horseback at the tail of a column on a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the great road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords often read its digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the biblical mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Leatherneck consuming fish spread

indicators.note: whatever consumes something has it inside

parts.note: leatherneck is American slang for a US Marine
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A Marine eating fish spread on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a verb but is the noun for something you put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that is spread on bread.

clue.text: Of little interest, it's what prep school boarders hope not to have

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for something unremarkable

definitions.text: it's what prep school boarders hope not to have
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, children at boarding school want news to put in letters to their parents

explanation.surface: A boarding-school child dreads having an empty week to report in the weekly letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A prep school is a private British primary school, often residential, where pupils traditionally wrote weekly letters home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something mediocre, not worth mentioning, and literally means having no news for a letter.

clue.text: Material in Missouri musical

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: Costume fabric used in a musical staged in Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric or yarn made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Ancient country's sources of news and information

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old kingdom of the Medes, in what is now Iran
second meaning: newspapers, broadcasting and the like

explanation.surface: Where an old nation gets its news.
explanation.definitionFit: Media was the kingdom of the Medes in antiquity, and the plural of medium names the press and broadcasters.

clue.text: Journalist finally leaving to inspire copy

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so it is taken out
finally points at the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A journalist finally quits to motivate the writing of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copy' looks like a journalist's text, but it is the verb meaning imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or mimic something, which is a sense of the verb copy.

clue.text: No longer listen to occupant of 29 protecting eastern boat

definitions.note: the answer is an archaic word for listen

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it

parts.note: 29 across is a poultry farm, which houses hens

explanation.surface: A hen sheltering a boat refuses to pay attention any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' tells you the definition is a dated word; the clue does not mean ceasing to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearken is an old-fashioned verb meaning to listen or pay heed, so it is listen in a sense now out of use.

clue.text: Celebrate homecoming, initially drawing flak at Little Chef, sadly

indicators.note: things going sadly go badly wrong, jumbling the letters
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: Little Chef is a British roadside restaurant chain

explanation.surface: A homecoming meal at a roadside diner gets a hostile reception.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the parable of the prodigal son, whose father had a calf killed to feast his return.

clue.text: Island school, one on a volcanic island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

explanation.surface: An island school sits on a volcanic island, a geography lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, off the coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: Doctor is at first doubtful about identifying diseases

parts.note: D stands for doctor in degrees such as DD

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: an agnostic is doubtful, especially about God

explanation.surface: A doctor starts off uncertain about what is wrong with a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal but simply supplies a single letter, and 'about' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnostic test or skill is one concerned with recognising illnesses from their symptoms.

clue.text: Dancing the reel where a lightweight car is seen

indicators.note: dancing sets the following words moving about

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance taking place where a tiny car is parked.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeler is a small, light motor vehicle with three wheels, such as the Reliant Robin.

clue.text: He is given years to absorb unknown US attorney's time of great success

indicators.note: absorbing something takes it inside

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A man gets a long prison term for taking in an American lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single-letter pieces for years and the unknown sit either side of the attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: A heyday is the peak period of someone's or something's power, popularity or vigour.

clue.text: King, for example, that is climbing Alpine height

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upward, from the bottom

explanation.surface: A monarch, say, scaling a mountain in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous mountain in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland, known for its north face.

clue.text: Some conveyancer testified truly of old

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A property lawyer gave evidence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: A conveyancer is a lawyer who handles the transfer of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Certes is an archaic adverb meaning certainly or assuredly, borrowed from Old French.

clue.text: Article on sacred river getting top grade

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: An essay about a holy river earns the best mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, is used as the highest mark in some grading schemes, as in alpha plus.

clue.text: A small country dwelling in Berkshire town?

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: A little rural cottage in a smart English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is a county west of London; the question mark flags that a cot is a poetic word for a cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, best known for its racecourse and the Royal Ascot meeting.

clue.text: King keeping almost new poultry farm

indicators.note: something keeping another holds it within

parts.note: Henry, the name of eight English kings

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A monarch keeping an almost-new chicken farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hennery is a place where hens are kept, a farm or run for poultry.

clue.text: Old character carrying a gun, a vagabond of yore

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
a gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A shady old man packing a pistol, a tramp from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' sounds like a person, but it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer, runaway or vagabond.

clue.text: Required to be worked in bakery, by the sound of it

indicators.note: points to how the words are spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: dough is pressed and worked by hand in a bakery

explanation.surface: Bread dough that needs to be worked by the baker.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed means wanted or necessary, so the past participle matches required.

clue.text: Church worker, perhaps, with writer's proclivity

parts.note: a pen is a writer, or what a writer uses
a worker ant, so an example

explanation.surface: A church employee who shares a writer's leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church worker' looks like one person; split it, and 'perhaps' marks the insect as an example of a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination for something, the same as a proclivity.

clue.text: Atmospheric layer the proposer somehow identifies

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tabling a motion names a part of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere, where weather happens.

clue.text: Cut first of ham in daze

indicators.note: in places that letter within the next word's equivalent
first of picks out the opening letter

explanation.surface: A dazed deli worker slicing ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' could be a verb, but it is a noun, a slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice of something, from the French for slice.

clue.text: US politician swindles island, acquiring Greek drugs

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in

explanation.surface: A corrupt American legislator runs scams on an island and buys Greek narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A congressman is a member of the US Congress, especially the House of Representatives.

clue.text: Discharge ambassador overcome by the hard stuff

indicators.note: something overcome by another is swamped and surrounded by it

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat dismissed after being overwhelmed by strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb meaning sack, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Intimate note found in can

indicators.note: something found in another is inside it

parts.note: may, as in you may go, means can
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A private message is discovered inside a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin, but it is the verb, as in be allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey describes a friendly, familiar manner, close in sense to intimate.

clue.text: One supports poor Bach suffering a fear of heights

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath what it holds up
something suffering is in a bad way, knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone props up the poor composer, who is terrified of heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrophobia is the medical term for an abnormal dread of high places, from Greek akron, summit.

clue.text: Mixed chorus here at monastery

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A choir of men and women sings at a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A charterhouse is a Carthusian monastery; the name is an English corruption of Chartreuse.

clue.text: Add a beat, ruining this rhyme

indicators.note: ruining something breaks it up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A poet complains that putting in an extra stress spoils the verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhythmise is to give something a rhythmic pattern, a regular metrical pulse.

clue.text: Organise distribution of blooms in Bury factory

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory

explanation.surface: Arranging flower deliveries from a works in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, so the capital disguises the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To interplant is to set plants among others, arranging how flowering crops are spread through a bed.

clue.text: A raver touring India, one providing scent

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a day

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it

parts.note: one who fumes, raving with anger

explanation.surface: A party-goer on a trip around India, supplying fragrances.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfumier makes or sells perfumes, so supplies scents.

clue.text: No seating for these key English dipping into treats?

indicators.note: something dipping into another goes inside it

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to treat them

explanation.surface: No chairs left for people helping themselves to sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treats' reads as a noun, sweets, but is the verb, as in buying a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Standees are people who stand, for instance at a show or on a bus, because no seats are left.

clue.text: Perform better than head of party, dividing cost

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it and sits in the gap
head of takes just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A party leader splits the bill and comes out ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay an opponent is to beat them by playing more skilfully.

clue.text: With trouble mounting, is willing to participate in casual affair

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising, read from the bottom up

parts.note: if you are on, you are game for it

explanation.surface: As problems grow, someone is ready to have a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a sexual relationship, typically a secret or short-lived one.

clue.text: Capsize plain vessel

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
a vessel for liquid or ashes

explanation.surface: An ordinary boat tips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' wants to be a ship; here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to turn something upside down, as a boat does when it capsizes.

clue.text: Honour like a knight in French city, missing grand reception at start

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
missing means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps
G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: at start picks out only the opening letter

parts.note: N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight is honoured in a French city but misses the big reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, or more loosely to dignify and honour them.

clue.text: Fairly nice to look at

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a lukewarm compliment, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means moderately or quite; as an adjective it means attractive in a delicate way.

clue.text: In places, twisted part of fourth raw nugget

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A misshapen piece of raw gold found in some spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' marks a regional word: this one is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrawn is a Scots word meaning crooked or misshapen, and also perverse or stubborn.

clue.text: Bear a grudge, having been caught in takeaway explosion?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for nursing resentment

definitions.text: having been caught in takeaway explosion
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, a fried potato from the blast has landed on your upper body

explanation.surface: Someone splattered when a fish and chip shop blew up holds a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: A takeaway is a fast-food shop; British chips are fried potato pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who stays resentful about a past slight and is quick to take offence.

clue.text: Outspoken gents, say, interrupted by commander contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily means the opposite way round
something interrupted by another has it break in

parts.note: a lav, short for lavatory, is a gents for example

explanation.surface: A commanding officer barges into a men's room in an awkward way.
explanation.walkthrough: Gents is British for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vocal expresses their opinions freely and forcefully, which is what outspoken means.

clue.text: Relaxation broken by current exam

indicators.note: something broken by another is split with it inside

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A break disrupted by the exam being sat now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective, but it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after a previous failure.

clue.text: Revert to bad habits, installing Liberal in seat

indicators.note: installing something puts it in place inside

explanation.surface: A politician relapses after a Liberal takes a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suggests Parliament, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad ways after trying to reform.

clue.text: Stoker eating last of flavoursome fish

indicators.note: something eating another has it inside
last of takes only the final letter

explanation.surface: A ship's boiler-man eats a tasty fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoker shovels coal into a furnace, but here it is the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream are freshwater or marine fish with deep, flattened bodies.

clue.text: Creatures originally seen with plates pointing backwards?

indicators.note: pointing backwards means facing the other way, so the whole is read right to left
originally means at the start, so the opening letter is used

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: Armoured beasts seen with their scales facing the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are living creatures, the general word for beasts as against plants.

clue.text: Completely exhausted ace left, returning no score

parts.note: A is ace on playing cards

indicators.note: returning means going back, so that word is read right to left

explanation.surface: A tennis player, worn out, loses without winning a point.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is a British informal phrase for utterly tired out.

clue.text: Missing organs primarily entertaining the old? Not so

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Is it entertaining to see old organs gone missing? Hardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeless means lacking eyes, which are organs of sight.

clue.text: Knight concerned with clairvoyant reportedly seeking no financial gain

parts.note: N is the knight in chess notation

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound counts

explanation.surface: A knight consults a fortune-teller with no thought of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The seer's word is pronounced identically to the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-profit organisation operates for a cause rather than to make money for owners.
